B. Is this measure already running in Satakunta wellbeing services county (or in the Tyks university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Video MDT review of every stage I-III patient with the university hospital. Every patient whose cancer has not spread (stage I-III) is discussed by video with the university hospital lung team (surgeon, radiotherapy doctor, oncologist) before anyone decides against treatment that aims to cure. Today a county hospital can decide alone.
effect_summary_en: In one English district hospital (62 patients in a year, before-after), the yearly resection rate rose by 30% (relative) after video MDT meetings began. The study gives no change in the curative share in percentage points.
supported_en: A 2004 study in the Journal of Telemedicine and Telecare reports a 30% relative rise in yearly resections after a video MDT with a thoracic surgeon started at a district hospital.
not_supported_en: The evidence does not show a 1.5-point rise in the share of all patients treated with curative intent, nor any effect in a setting like Finland's.
in_use_quote: Satasairaalan lääkärit osallistuvat kokouksiin etäyhteydellä. Kaikkia syöpätapauksia ei ole tarpeellista käsitellä kokouksessa, vaan hoitosuunnitelma laaditaan kansalliseen hoitosuositukseen perustuen.
in_use_summary_en: Tyks says its multidisciplinary lung team meets every week and Satasairaala doctors join by remote link. Tyks also says not every cancer case needs to go to the meeting.
missing_en: No page shows a rule that every stage I–III patient must be discussed before anyone decides against curative treatment.
summary_en: Tyks says its multidisciplinary lung team (lung doctors, surgeon, radiotherapy, pathology and radiology doctors) meets every week, Satasairaala doctors join by remote link, and not every cancer case is discussed at the meeting. So the video link already exists, but no rule makes every stage I–III patient go to the meeting. For the effect, a 2004 English before-after study of 62 patients found yearly resections rose by 30% (relative) after video MDT meetings started; it does not measure a change in the curative share in percentage points.
unanswered_en: I found no page on how many Satakunta stage I–III patients are discussed at the Tyks meeting today, and no recent study measuring a change in the curative share.
